A1.justification: Both PDFs are 119-page versions of the Apertus technical report. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–P support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Apertus benchmark evaluations, architecture and training ablations, memorization experiments, and a Swiss AI Charter survey, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional checkpoint evaluations in Figure 7 and long-context scores in Table 23.

M1.justification: Table 1 revises the reported Apertus-70B hidden dimension from 4096 to 8192. This is a localized architecture-specification correction; the PDFs do not establish retraining or a new model procedure. The architecture components and training algorithms otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training corpora, evaluation tasks, languages, and domains remain unchanged. The additional checkpoint and RULER scores concern existing benchmark coverage; 32k and 64k contexts were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged. SmolLM3-3B already has a plotted endpoint in v1 Figure 7; v2 adds its intermediate checkpoints. Table 23 retains the same model rows.

E3.justification: Table 12 corrects the reported Swiss Charter Q&A training-example count from 943,427 to 226, making it consistent with the unchanged regional subtotal of 943,427. This revises a stated sample count without establishing that training data or experiments actually changed.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the analysis of performance over pretraining by adding SmolLM3-3B intermediate-checkpoint trajectories for global, English, EU, and Swiss evaluations, where v1 showed endpoints only. The architecture, filtering, and Goldfish ablations and memorization robustness analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical procedures are unchanged. The additional checkpoint and RULER results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds SmolLM3-3B checkpoint results. Table 23 fills seven missing RULER cells, including 64k scores of 56.9 for Apertus-70B and 67.3 for Apertus-70B-Instruct, and changes SmolLM3-3B's 64k score from 66.0 to 65.9. These are added or corrected results, rather than demonstrated improvements to the Apertus models.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 changes the displayed Goldfish-loss factor from G_i x_i to G_i(x_i), a localized correction to the formal loss expression. The accompanying masking procedure, Appendix F algorithm, QRPO derivation, and other mathematical definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, principal contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about scale, openness, data compliance, multilingual capability, and memorization mitigation.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning compliance tradeoffs, memorization, multilingual performance, safety, and deployment remain unchanged. The additional results receive no new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Table C.4 newly specifies an initialization standard deviation of 0.008944. v2 also adds a posttraining-data repository entry and an explicit access link for the SFT mixture in Section 4.1.3. These improve documentation without establishing changed initialization or training procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds Foroutan et al. (2025c), Revisiting Multilingual Data Mixtures in Language Model Pretraining, to the related-publications list and bibliography. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited: v2 removes a duplicated sentence from Table 6's caption, adjusts punctuation, and updates front matter and cross-references. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 7 adds checkpoint curves within its existing panels. Table 23 moves the context-length unit into individual column labels, Table C.4 gains a row, and Table 13 moves from page 35 to page 36. Other differences mainly involve local reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting accuracy and reproducibility through corrected architecture and sample-count entries, an initialization detail, explicit data-access information, and fuller evaluation results. The gains are limited, and Table 23 retains an inconsistent runtime-failure caption despite now reporting the Apertus-70B-Instruct 64k score. Overall, the corrections and additional evidence provide a modest quality improvement.
